memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'because of your father's God, who helps you, because of the Almighty, who blesses you with blessings of the skies above, blessings of the deep springs below, blessings of the breast and womb. Your father's blessings are greater than the blessings of the ancient mountains, than the bounty of the age-old hills. Let all these rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince among his brothers.'" — Gen 49:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob piles up the language of abundance. Blessings from the skies above, the deep springs below, the breast and womb — rain, water, children. Everything a family in that world needed to flourish. Greater, he says, than the ancient mountains.

And notice where every one of them originates: "because of your father's God, who helps you, because of the Almighty, who blesses you."

That phrase is the anchor of the whole passage. The blessings are not Jacob's to give. He is asking God to give them.

This matters, because it keeps us from a serious error. Scripture does not teach that God's people are guaranteed material abundance — Joseph's own life included slavery and prison, and his descendants would be enslaved in Egypt. Blessings of skies and springs are real gifts, and God does give them, but they are not a contract we can hold Him to.

James reminds us that every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father of lights (Jas 1:17). The right response to any good thing in your life is to look up.

And the greatest blessing God gives is not rain or children. It is Himself, in Christ — every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms (Eph 1:3).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What good things in your life have you stopped thanking God for?
2. Do you treat God's blessings as gifts or as entitlements?
3. What does it mean to you that the greatest blessing is God Himself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, every good thing in my life came from You. Forgive me for taking Your gifts for granted, and thank You that the greatest gift is knowing You. Amen.
